TOCTOU (Time-of-Check to Time-of-Use) Race in start_pty_process Alias Registration

The alias uniqueness check and the actual registration in self._processes are in two separate lock acquisitions. A second call with the same alias arriving between the two with self._lock blocks would pass the uniqueness check and both calls would register, with the second overwriting the first's child and log_fh without closing them.

Suggestion fix is to Open the file and spawn the process outside the lock (they're blocking I/O), then perform a second check-and-set inside the final lock acquisition before writing to the dicts

```
with self._lock:
    if alias in self._processes:  # re-check inside lock
        child.close(force=True)
        log_fh.close()
        raise RuntimeError(
            "A PTY process with alias '{}' is already running. "
            "Stop it first with 'Stop PTY Process'.".format(alias)
        )
    self._processes[alias] = child
    self._log_handles[alias] = log_fh
    self._log_paths[alias] = log_file
```

Prevents silently leaked file handles and orphaned child processes in concurrent suite execution scenarios.

import signal Inside Method Body

Move import signal to Line 23 alongside the other top-level imports.

Improves readability and static analysis (e.g., pylint, mypy will not flag an "import not at top of file" warning).

Hardcoded Device-Specific HOST_COMMAND_PROMPT

This variable embeds a specific device hostname (raspberrypi-4f8b). The SSH test asserts Should Contain ${output} ${HOST_COMMAND_PROMPT} in the Verify Standalone SOL output from DCSCM using SBC over SSH test case, which will always fail on any hardware other than this exact RPI unit.

Suggestion fix is to Make HOST_COMMAND_PROMPT an externally supplied variable with a generic default, or widen the assertion to match a broader pattern:

```
${HOST_COMMAND_PROMPT}       qualcomm@      # matches any qualcomm@<hostname>
```

Hardcoded device identifiers are a portability anti-pattern that will cause immediate failures in CI or on any other EVB+RPI configuration

Either you do it in one place, Test teardown or Suite Teardown for this case thats the first one.. 

Next,

These Terminate Process calls reference handle names (sol_proc, sol_tc06, sol_client1, sol_client2) from Robot Framework's built-in Process library, but none of the test cases in this suite start processes via Process.Start Process using those handles. All sessions are managed exclusively via the PTY library. These calls are dead code left over from an earlier implementation.

What we should do is Remove the four Terminate Process lines from both Suite Teardown Execution and Test Teardown Execution, leaving only Stop All PTY Processes for session cleanup.

Dead code adds noise, misleads future maintainers, and could mask a legitimate process leak by absorbing errors silently (Run Keyword And Ignore Error).
